author: liam.oconnor - Sports Editor
title: Swan Delisted: Injury Ends AFL Career | News
text:
Swans Announce List Changes Following Disappointing 2025 Season A difficult period of list management has begun for the Sydney Swans, with the club announcing the delisting of four players after falling short of finals contention in the 2025 season. The moves signal a clear intent to reshape the roster following a 10th-place finish.
Key Departures Include Veteran Fox and Kirk
Among those departing are Robbie Fox , a versatile tall who played 105 games for the club, and Indhi Kirk , the son of Swans legend Brett Kirk. Also delisted were Caleb Mitchell and Ben Paton . The decisions, while difficult, were framed as necessary by club officials.
Fox’s journey to the top level was particularly notable, rising from suburban football in Melbourne after originally hailing from Tasmania. He proved a reliable performer, featuring in both the 2022 and 2024 Grand Finals – notably, one of the few Swans players to perform admirably in those championship losses. Unfortunately, a significant injury derailed his 2025 season, limiting him to a handful of appearances in the VFL, with his last senior game being the 2024 Grand Final defeat against Brisbane.
Paton joined the Swans in the previous off-season after being released by St Kilda, managing four senior games this year. Mitchell, drafted with pick 40 in 2022, saw limited opportunities, playing just three senior games across three seasons. Kirk, a product of the Swans Academy, accumulated 43 VFL appearances but did not break into the senior side.
“It’s always a really difficult time of year when we need to make these list decisions,” a senior club official stated. “Robbie, Caleb, Indhi and Ben have all made significant contributions to the Swans through their time here at the club. We are very grateful for their hard work and commitment.”
The official further emphasized Fox’s impact, stating, “Robbie, in particular, will be remembered fondly within the footy club having played over 100 games for us which is no small achievement.”
The club expressed its best wishes to all four players as they embark on the next chapter of their careers. The Swans will now turn their attention to the upcoming draft and trade periods as they look to rebuild and return to premiership contention.
